Evaluating integration strategies for Next.js and Vite.

Standard Next.js App Router will serve as the primary framework. Vite will be integrated for component development rather than as the main bundler.

Node.js 24.x LTS will be the runtime environment. Vite will be retained for shared UI package builds and component development.

Next.js will use the App Router with React and JavaScript. Vite will handle development tooling such as local component development and API proxying. Environment variables will follow Next.js conventions using NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefixes instead of VITE_.

The documentation will be kept simple. The stack is React, Next.js (App Router), and JavaScript. Vite will be documented only as a fallback for specific tasks.

Next.js 14+ does not officially support Vite. The stack will be documented as React, Next.js, Vite, and JavaScript. Node.js 24.x Active LTS will be pinned in `.nvmrc` and `engines`.

JavaScript ES modules will replace TypeScript entirely. Environment variables will migrate from VITE_* to NEXT_PUBLIC_* for Next.js compatibility. Vite will be preserved for a dedicated proxy subproject. The scope covers rules, specifications, commands, constitution, cursor rules, architecture, UI flow, and review commands.

A monorepo layout is being considered for frontend.md, though an isolated Vite directory was rejected as a poor fit. Architecture and DEC-15 requirements will be reviewed for full updates. The plan is to keep Next.js as the primary application shell and reserve Vite for local development utilities.

Vite will be reserved for shared library and design-system packages built in library mode and imported into the Next.js application. It will remain approved for component packages and development tooling within the frontend directory. Next.js will serve as the primary application shell.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Checking the specstory file and related documentation to understand the planned frontend stack update.

Next.js App Router will serve as the primary application shell and routing layer. Vite will be configured for a shared component library or the development server. Node.js 24.x Active LTS is selected. The frontend will use JavaScript with ES modules and React function components. TypeScript will be excluded from the frontend.

Simplifying the architecture. Next.js App Router will be the primary frontend application. Vite will handle the development API proxy to the backend. A separate Vite dev server may support standalone component work.

Next.js will use `next.config` rewrites to proxy API requests instead of a separate Vite proxy. Vite will be reserved for building the HTTP API client package or optional Storybook. Hybrid React and Next.js setups were rejected. The frontend documentation will specify Node.js 24.x Active LTS and JavaScript with no TypeScript.

Vite will build shared modules such as the API client and presentational components inside `frontend/`. Next.js will import these modules while handling routing, SSR, and production bundling. A second SPA entry point will be avoided unless the specification explicitly requires it.

Environment variables will be split between the two tools. Next.js will use `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` for client-side configuration. Vite will use `import.meta.env` for its own package configuration.

Two directory layouts are being considered. One keeps the Next.js App Router in a `next-app/` subdirectory and places shared components in `packages/ui/`. The alternative flattens the structure into `app/` and `src/api/`.

A `vite.config.js` will be added for Vite library mode. Existing documentation is being checked for frontend environment variable conventions to decide whether to unify on `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefixes or keep separate Vite variables.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

The frontend stack is now documented and wired as **React + Next.js + Vite + JavaScript** on **Node.js 24.x Active LTS (Krypton)**. There was no `frontend/` app yet, so changes are rules, specs, tooling stubs, and backend CORS.

### Stack (DEC-15 revised)

| Layer | Choice |
|--------|--------|
| **Node** | **24.x** Active LTS — `frontend/.nvmrc` (`24`), `frontend/package.json` `engines` |
| **Language** | **JavaScript** (`.js`/`.jsx`; no TypeScript in frontend) |
| **React** | Function components |
| **Next.js** | App Router — pages, routing, production build (`localhost:3000`) |
| **Vite** | Shared `frontend/src/` modules (especially API client), HMR/proxy (`localhost:5173`) |

**Env:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (Next) and optional `VITE_API_BASE_URL` (Vite dev) — see `frontend/.env.example`.

### Files updated

- **Source of truth:** `rules/frontend.md` (full rewrite of stack, layout, env, examples)
- **Specs:** `spec/requirements.md` (OQ-09, **DEC-15**), `spec/architecture.md` (§7, §10.4, §12, §18), `spec/ui-flow.md`
- **Commands / rules:** `commands/review-frontend.md`, `review-code.md`, `review-spec.md`, `rules/documentation.md`, `rules/java-springboot.md` (CORS example)
- **Steering:** `.cursor/rules/frontend.mdc`, `java-tech-lead-sdd.mdc`, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `docs/assessment-brief.md`, `skills/documentation/SKILL.md`, `plan.md`
- **Backend:** `WebCorsConfig.java` — allows **`http://localhost:3000`** and **`http://localhost:5173`**
- **Scaffold:** `frontend/.nvmrc`, `frontend/package.json`, `frontend/.env.example`

### How Next + Vite fit together

Next.js owns **routes and the production bundle** (`frontend/app/`). Vite supports **shared JavaScript** under `frontend/src/` (HTTP client, components) with optional dev proxy—without a second SPA unless a spec adds one.

When you implement the UI, add Next/Vite dependencies and scripts to `frontend/package.json`; only Node pinning exists today.

If you want **Next only** (drop Vite from the convention) or **Vite-only SPA** (drop Next), say which and we can align DEC-15 again.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Closed the remaining **draft / Open** gaps and aligned steering docs with the **agreed** ten-file spec set. Summary:

### New decision: **DEC-20** (UI routes, layout, interaction)

Recorded in [`spec/requirements.md`](spec/requirements.md) §10.2 and [`spec/ui-flow.md`](spec/ui-flow.md) §4, §7, §14:

| Topic | Agreed choice |
|--------|----------------|
| **Routes** | Next.js App Router: `/` → `/tickets`, `/tickets`, `/tickets/new`, `/tickets/[id]`, `/ask` |
| **Ask** | Dedicated **`/ask`** page + nav links from list/detail (no drawer-only UX in v1) |
| **Styling** | Plain CSS (global or CSS modules); no Tailwind/MUI in v1 |
| **List search** | Apply button + Enter |
| **Pagination** | Prev/next + page numbers from `meta` |
| **Create** | **201** → navigate to new ticket detail |
| **Detail** | Single **Save changes** for fields (no `status` in that PATCH); legal statuses as separate button group |
| **Citations** | Ticket id links/chips to detail |
| **Component file names** | Still implementer choice |

**DEC-15** now points at **DEC-20** for UX (stack unchanged: React + Next.js + Vite + JS, Node 24 LTS).

### Other Open items closed

- Hub: validation **400** paths, FEAT-19 config via **DEC-16** `application.yml`, pagination/search prose, FEAT-11/17/18 UI ownership, citations layout → **DEC-20**
- **DEC-12** auth: no auth (**Agreed**); updated in architecture, data-model, rag-api-contract (**Reference** for auth/SSE)
- State machine: illegal **status** fails whole PATCH (**Agreed**)
- Architecture §12: navigation aligned with **DEC-20**; ingest-version **Open** removed
- Steering: [`docs/assessment-brief.md`](docs/assessment-brief.md) §4 all **agreed**; §7 **Boot 4 / Java 25**; **DEC-01…20**
- [`skills/documentation/SKILL.md`](skills/documentation/SKILL.md), [`rules/documentation.md`](rules/documentation.md), [`commands/generate-tests.md`](commands/generate-tests.md), [`commands/review-spec.md`](commands/review-spec.md), [`commands/review-frontend.md`](commands/review-frontend.md), [`commands/review-code.md`](commands/review-code.md), [`rules/api-standards.md`](rules/api-standards.md), [`rules/frontend.md`](rules/frontend.md), [`plan.md`](plan.md) — **DEC-01…20** / agreed spec set

### What “Open” still means in docs

Only the **label legend** (“Open = unresolved until DEC…”) and **Reference** out-of-scope items (e.g. async ingest queue, auth). **No blocking Open rows** in §10.2.

---

You can proceed to the **frontend implementation plan** against **DEC-15 + DEC-20**, `ui-flow.md`, and API contracts. If you want different UX (e.g. ask as a panel instead of `/ask`), say so and we can revise **DEC-20** before you plan.
